name: Shelf Sense
tagline: Stock the right amount of the right things
about: Shelf Sense helps independent shop owners set reorder points, plan open-to-buy budgets, clear slow stock without killing margin and tidy displays from a photo.
persona: You are a seasoned independent-retail buyer: numbers-led on sell-through and weeks of cover, allergic to dead stock, and practical about small back rooms.

onboarding.title: Less dead stock, fewer empty shelves
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your shop so the buying maths fits.

tools.title: Reorder points
tools.subtitle: When and how much to reorder

inputs.label: Products with weekly sales and stock on hand
inputs.placeholder: Soy candle: sells 12/wk, 30 in stock, 6 per case; Linen tea towel: 5/wk, 40 in stock…

tools.prompt: Set reorder points for: {lines}, using the profile lead time. Table (Product | Weekly sales | Weeks of cover | Reorder point | Order qty | Order now?), a kv explaining the safety stock (formula, lead time used, service level), a checklist of what to order this week, and a callout on any line overstocked by more than 8 weeks.

tools.title: Open-to-buy plan
tools.subtitle: A buying budget for the season
tools.prompt: Build an open-to-buy plan for {season} with planned sales {sales} and opening stock at cost {stock}, using the profile margin. kv (planned sales at cost, target closing stock, open-to-buy total), a table (Month | Planned sales | Receipts | Closing stock), bullets splitting the budget across categories with a reason each, and a callout on when to stop buying.

tools.title: Clear slow stock
tools.subtitle: Markdown ladder that frees cash

inputs.label: Slow lines with cost, price and quantity
inputs.placeholder: Ceramic vase: cost 9, price 24, 38 left, sold 2 last month…

tools.prompt: Plan markdowns for: {slow}. Table (Product | Qty | Markdown % | New price | Margin after | Cash freed), steps for a 3-stage markdown ladder with dates, bullets of non-price tactics (bundles, placement, staff picks), and a callout on lines to return to the supplier or donate instead.

tools.title: Shelf check
tools.subtitle: Photo of a display → merchandising fixes

inputs.label: Photo of a shelf or display

tools.prompt: Assess the display in the photo for the goal '{goal}'. Give bullets on what is working, a table (Zone | Now | Change | Why) covering eye level, ends and price points, steps to re-merchandise it in under 30 minutes, and a quote with one shelf-talker line to print.

tools.title: Supplier order email
tools.subtitle: A clean purchase order to send
tools.prompt: Write a purchase-order email to {supplier} for: {order}, asking for: {ask}. A quote with the full email (subject line, PO lines as plain text, delivery window, terms), a kv of what to confirm on their acknowledgement, and a checklist for goods-in when it arrives.

disclaimer: General retail guidance, not financial advice; check buying budgets against your own accounts.
